comparison.title: Why not Excel, Splitwise, or notes?
comparison.subtitle: OurMoney is the only tool designed specifically for couples - not roommates, not groups.

items.question: Do we both need to have the app?
items.answer: Not at the start! One of you can try the app first, and when you're ready - invite your partner and start using it together. This way you get 100% out of it without needing both of you on board from day one!

items.question: Is the app free?
items.answer: The app is completely free - no credit card, no limits. When we introduce paid plans, existing users will be the first to know and will get special terms.

items.question: How does expense splitting work?
items.answer: You can choose from four options: 50/50 split or proportional to income (e.g. 60/40 if one of you earns more). OurMoney automatically calculates who should contribute what. You can also track without a set split, or use a predetermined budget.

items.question: Does the app work on iOS and Android?
items.answer: OurMoney is a Progressive Web App (PWA) - it works on any device through the browser. You can add it to your home screen just like a native app. One account, access everywhere!

items.question: How do I install OurMoney on my phone?
items.answer: OurMoney is a PWA - you install it straight from your browser, no App Store or Google Play needed. On iPhone: open app.ourmoney.pl in Safari, tap the share icon and choose 'Add to Home Screen'. On Android: open the site in Chrome and pick 'Install app' from the menu. Once installed, OurMoney works like a regular app - with its own icon and offline support.

items.question: Will our data be secure?
items.answer: Privacy and security are our top priority. We apply the highest standards of data protection.

meta.description: See how much each of you should pay when you earn different amounts. Income-proportional split versus 50/50 - instant result, no signup.

CalculatorPage.title: Expense split calculator for unequal incomes
CalculatorPage.subtitle: Enter your incomes and shared costs. You will see the fair share for each of you and how much more the lower earner pays under a 50/50 split.
CalculatorPage.howTitle: How we calculate the fair split
CalculatorPage.howBody: Each of you covers the same percentage of shared expenses as your income represents in your joint income. With salaries of 6500 zl and 4500 zl the joint income is 11 000 zl, so the shares are 59% and 41%. With 4000 zl of shared expenses that means 2360 zl and 1640 zl instead of 2000 zl each.

faq.question: Is a proportional split fairer than 50/50?
faq.answer: When incomes differ a lot, a 50/50 split hits the lower earner much harder - after the shared bills they have far less money left. A proportional split evens out that burden. There is no single right answer, what matters is choosing a rule deliberately and both agreeing to it.

faq.question: How do we count income when it is irregular?
faq.answer: Use the average of the last three to six months. With large swings (freelance, commission) it is easier to set the proportions once a quarter than to recalculate every month.

faq.question: Does OurMoney do this automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. You set the splitting rule once and every shared expense is divided automatically - proportionally to income, equally, or by your own custom proportions. You also see who has already paid how much.
